    AI Overview
    Pershing Square USA, Ltd. (PSUS) is a newly launched Delaware-based closed-end investment company managed by Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square Capital Management. It aims to provide a permanent capital model for investing in large-cap, North American-headquartered companies. The company is planning a combined IPO of PSUS shares and Pershing Square Inc. (PSI) in 2026, aiming to raise up to $10 billion. 
    Key details about Pershing Square USA include: 
    • Initial Public Offering (IPO): As of April 2026, PSUS is conducting a dual IPO, where investors can purchase shares, with plans to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "PSUS".
    • Structure: Designed to be a listed closed-end fund, aiming to emulate a "Berkshire Hathaway-style" permanent capital structure to reduce redemption risks.
    • Investment Goal: The fund intends to pursue long-term capital appreciation by investing in high-quality companies, often with significant operations in the United States.
    • Management: Managed by Pershing Square Capital Management, L.P. (PSCM), with Bill Ackman as a key figure. 
    Note: This refers to the financial entity "Pershing Square USA Ltd.", not the public park in Los Angeles.

    What is Pershing Square known for?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Pershing Square Capital Management, founded by Bill Ackman in 2004, is a premier activist hedge fund known for managing a concentrated portfolio of large-cap, high-quality, cash-generative businesses. It is renowned for high-profile activist campaigns aimed at driving strategic, operational, and management changes to create long-term shareholder value. 
    Key Aspects of Pershing Square:
    • Activist Hedge Fund:
      Founded by Bill Ackman, the firm takes large positions in companies (typically 8–12 core holdings) and pushes for changes, such as in its high-profile campaigns against companies like Target and Herbalife. 
    • Concentrated Strategy:
      Focused on "predictable, durable growth businesses," taking substantial stakes and engaging actively with management. 
    • High-Profile Investments:
      Notable positions include Herbalife, Canadian Pacific Railway, Chipotle Mexican Grill, and Universal Music Group. 
    • Performance Fluctuations:
      Known for high-stakes, sometimes controversial campaigns that have led to significant gains or notable losses, reflecting the high risk of activism. 
    Note: This refers to Pershing Square Capital Management (the hedge fund). There is also a famous public park (Pershing Square in Los Angeles) and a building (Pershing Square Building in New York).

      What is Warren Buffett's 70/30 rule?
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      The Warren Buffett 70/30 rule is an investment strategy recommending a portfolio allocation of 70% in growth assets (stocks/equities) and 30% in defensive assets (bonds or fixed income). It aims to balance high long-term growth with volatility protection, allowing investors to stay invested during market downturns. 
      Key Details of the 70/30 Rule
      • Purpose:
        Provides a "middle-ground" approach between high-risk (100% stocks) and low-risk (conservative) portfolios. 
      • Origin:
        Often associated with a 1957 letter where Buffett noted a 70% stock and 30% "corporate workout" (special situation) allocation. It is widely interpreted today as 70% Stocks / 30% Bonds. 
      • Ideal User:
        Suitable for long-term investors seeking growth while reducing the impact of market crashes. 
      • Flexibility:
        While 70/30 is popular, many investors modify it based on age or risk appetite (e.g., 80/20 for younger, 50/50 for retirees). 
      Benefits
      • Growth + Stability:
        The 70% in stocks allows for significant appreciation, while the 30% in bonds cushions against losses. 
      • "Sleep Well" Ratio:
        It offers enough growth to beat inflation but enough safety to prevent panic selling. 
      Disclaimer: This is a general investing guideline. Individual risk tolerance and financial goals should be considered.

        Does Bill Ackman still support Trump?
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        Yes, as of late 2024 and through 2025, billionaire investor Bill Ackman officially endorsed and supported Donald Trump for the 2024 election. The Pershing Square CEO stated that a Trump win was in the "best interest of the country" and has criticized the Democratic Party's leadership, calling it "fundamentally undemocratic". 
        Key details of his support:
        • Formal Endorsement:
          Ackman endorsed Trump in July 2024 following the assassination attempt, stating he would help the president succeed, though not in an official capacity. 
        • "Pro-Business" Focus:
          He described Trump as "most pro-business president we've ever had," believing a Trump administration is beneficial for the economy and financial markets. 
        • Shifting Politics:
          A long-time Democratic donor, Ackman pivoted to supporting Republican candidates and criticizing the Democratic Party in the 2024 election cycle, particularly regarding policies on free markets and border security. 
        • Continued Alignment:
          In 2025, Ackman continued to act as a vocal supporter, engaging in "very-online" commentary as a "Trump-loving culture warrior". 
        As of early 2026, Ackman remains active in supporting pro-business, anti-socialist, and anti-far-left policies.
